newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND UPS INTERVENTION WHEAT BUYING LIMIT.
newsitem.headline: POLAND UPS INTERVENTION WHEAT BUYING LIMIT.

text.p: The Polish government cleared a plan on Tuesday to increase state intervention wheat purchase this year by 100,000 tonnes of bread wheat, a deputy agriculture minister said.

"The government authorised the Farm Market Agency (ARR) to intervene through purchases of consumption wheat not exceeding 100,000 tonnes with a focus on small and medium-sized farms," Jerzy Pilarczyk told a news briefing.

He said the government approved a maximum intervention price for wheat at 530 zlotys per tonne. Last week the average wheat price on Poland's farm markets was 546 zlotys per tonne and it traded at 540 zlotys on Poland's physical commodity exchanges.
Earlier on Monday the government spokeswoman said ARR was requesting a 200,000 tonne increase in wheat purchases.

The government has said the purchase would be designed to help farmers, who find it unprofitable to sell their grain because storage facilities are full after substantial imports last year and early in 1997.
Under an earlier plan, ARR was to buy 487,800 tonnes of wheat this year, of which 180,000 tonnes would be imported, and 52,500 tonnes of rye.
